description:
Returns statistical distributions of weather attributes (temperature, precipitation, wind, etc.) for a location and time period.
When to use: Establish the climatological baseline — what is 'normal' for this location and period. Use before discussing anomalies.
Date format: YYYY[MM[DD]]: YYYYMMDD for a specific week, YYYYMM for a month, YYYY for a seasonal or annual overview. Note: YYYYMMDD does not give info about daily obs. If a date is specified it corresponds to the week. Use /events for daily history.
Performance: Computed on demand; moderate speed. Avoid date spans wider than one year.
Prerequisites: Use /location to obtain a locid first.
Investigate: Good for grounding anomaly claims — e.g. 'Is 35°C in July unusual for Madrid?' Check distributions before asserting extremeness.
Augment: Use to provide climatological context before describing observed anomalies in an article. Returns: duration, observations, conditions, probs, pcps, means, >>.
